scenarios.title: Modeled Link-State Lifecycle
scenarios.summary: A standards-structured lab scenario showing an interface transition from baseline through recovery.

scenarios.title: Cisco IOS XR Interface Degradation — Golden Scenario
scenarios.summary: An evidence-bounded Cisco 8000 IOS XR scenario correlating documented interface syslog, IF-MIB SNMP, and OpenConfig gNMI from one shared enterprise state plan.

scenarios.title: Campus Access Link Degradation — IOS XE Reference
scenarios.summary: The reference emits an ordered IOS XE interface lifecycle over the bundled native syslog receiver and then the separate HEC destination path.

scenarios.title: Nexus Fabric Uplink Degradation — NX-OS Reference
scenarios.summary: The reference selects documented NX-OS ETHPORT message structures by lifecycle phase without inventing speed or mode suffixes.

scenarios.title: Secure Firewall Suspicious Connection Burst — ASA Reference
scenarios.summary: The reference emits Cisco-documented ASA 302013 and 302014 structures with reserved addresses. Rate change is modeled; malicious intent is not asserted.

scenarios.title: Telecom Operations Network Degradation — Correlated Reference
scenarios.summary: IOS XE and IOS XR source-native syslog structures are generated from one shared state lifecycle while retaining independent device and interface identities.

scenarios.title: DNS Diversity and NXDOMAIN Indicators

scenarios.title: Periodic External Communication Indicators

scenarios.title: Internal Reconnaissance Indicators
scenarios.summary: Identify a bounded rise in internal destination and port diversity.

scenarios.title: DNS Tunneling and Exfiltration Indicators
scenarios.summary: Identify synthetic long-subdomain and DNS-flow indicators without performing or claiming exfiltration.

scenarios.title: Cross-Source DNS, Beaconing, and Reconnaissance Incident

scenarios.title: Supply Chain to Application

scenarios.title: CAN: Campus Area Network - Multi-Building Backbone & Catalyst Center
scenarios.summary: Multi-building campus network with redundant Catalyst 9600 cores, 100G fiber interconnects, and DNA Center automated assurance. A multi-building campus loses the primary uplink of one building distribution switch; the distribution switch logs the uplink failure and recovery, Catalyst Center network-health samples are replayed, and TrustSec SGT propagation across the affected path degrades and then recovers.

scenarios.title: EPN: Enterprise Private Network - Isolated Corporate Intranet & Multi-Cloud VPC
scenarios.summary: A branch access switch, provider-edge router, SD-WAN edge and cloud VPC gateway form a private QinQ/MPLS intranet. A double-tagged 802.1ad frame (VLAN hopping attempt) hits the branch access port; the outer S-VLAN is stripped and a hardware ACL drops the inner encapsulation while the SD-WAN path stays healthy.

scenarios.title: GAN: Global Area Network - Worldwide Multi-Cloud & Subsea Cable Transit
scenarios.summary: A subsea landing-station router carries traffic between AWS Direct Connect and Azure ExpressRoute edges. An undersea seismic event degrades optical signal quality on the lambda; interface throughput falls, Zscaler inspection latency and ThousandEyes probe latency and loss climb, and a fast-protection switch moves traffic to the terrestrial fallback before service returns to normal.

scenarios.title: LAN: Local Area Network - Campus Switching & 802.1Q Segments
scenarios.summary: High-density campus LAN with Cisco Catalyst 9300/9500 switches, 802.1Q trunking, DHCP snooping, and ARP inspection.

scenarios.title: MAN: Metropolitan Area Network - 100G Carrier Ethernet Ring & G.8032 ERPS
scenarios.summary: Metro optical ring spanning 4 data centers with ITU-T G.8032 Ethernet Ring Protection Switching (ERPS) sub-50ms failover.

scenarios.title: NAS: Network-Attached Storage - NetApp ONTAP & PowerScale Clusters
scenarios.summary: High-throughput NAS cluster serving petabyte NFSv4.1 and SMB3 workloads with IOPS burst tracking and volume latency metrics. An Arista switch pair carries NAS traffic for a NetApp ONTAP / PowerScale cluster; latency on the NAS export rises and clients are affected until the storage path recovers.

scenarios.title: PAN: Personal Area Network - IoT Sensor Cluster & Bluetooth Mesh
scenarios.summary: Short-range IoT sensor mesh monitoring environmental conditions, temperature, humidity, and Bluetooth LE beacon telemetry. A cluster of Bluetooth IoT sensors reports through a gateway; sensor reporting drops and the gateway logs link trouble before the mesh recovers.

scenarios.title: SAN: Storage Area Network - Cisco MDS 9700 Fibre Channel & NVMe-oF
scenarios.summary: Enterprise storage area network fabric with Cisco MDS 9700 64G FC directors, zoning, and buffer-to-buffer credit starvation telemetry. A Cisco Nexus fabric switch shows buffer pressure on a storage-facing port while a Fibre Channel path degrades; pressure peaks, the path is moved, and the fabric recovers.

scenarios.title: VPN: Virtual Private Network - Cisco AnyConnect & Site-to-Site IPsec
scenarios.summary: Remote access VPN concentrator and IPsec crypto tunnels supporting 10,000+ concurrent workforce sessions with Duo MFA integration.

scenarios.title: WAN: Wide Area Network - Global BGP/MPLS L3VPN Backbone & Optical DWDM
scenarios.summary: Inter-continental provider-edge routers (Cisco IOS-XR) and a Juniper core router carry a BGP/MPLS L3VPN backbone. Trans-oceanic latency degrades: a BGP session to the core flaps and IOS-XR engages TI-LFA fast reroute, the Juniper core moves its MPLS RSVP-TE LSP to the bypass path, and the backbone then returns to its primary path.

scenarios.title: WLAN: Wireless Local Area Network - Catalyst 9800 & Meraki Wi-Fi 6E/7
scenarios.summary: Dual-vendor campus wireless with Catalyst 9800 WLC and Meraki MR56 APs tracking client roaming, SNR, and CleanAir interference.

scenarios.title: Data Center Fabric ACI Ingress Microburst Traffic
scenarios.summary: Microburst traffic pattern saturates Nexus 9K leaf switch ingress ASIC buffers; ACI fabric health score drops and MDT telemetry flags queue incast.

scenarios.title: Campus Core L2/3 Disturbance & Rogue AP
scenarios.summary: Unsanctioned Rogue AP connects to campus switch; Cisco ISE applies 802.1X quarantine while Catalyst core detects MAC flapping.

scenarios.title: Enterprise WAN Circuit Brownout & App Route Failover
scenarios.summary: MPLS transport experiences high latency and packet loss; Cisco SD-WAN vEdge triggers SLA violation and BGP failover to secondary LTE/Broadband.

scenarios.title: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS SYN Flood)
scenarios.summary: Malicious botnet IPs launch high-rate TCP SYN floods targeting internal infrastructure.

scenarios.title: Ransomware / Lateral Spread (Port 445)
scenarios.summary: A compromised application server tries to spread over SMB (TCP/445) to other internal servers while privileged catalog queries appear against the database. A segmentation ASA denies the cross-subnet SMB flows, the core switch records the denied traffic, and database access returns to normal application queries.

scenarios.title: Multicast/MPLS Backbone Optical Carrier Shift
scenarios.summary: DWDM Loss-of-Signal alarm on Nokia SR-OS core triggers Juniper Junos RSVP-TE Fast Reroute (FRR) switchover; Arista IPFIX telemetry tracks rerouted flow.

scenarios.title: Distributed Edge Breach & Internal Probing
scenarios.summary: Attacker probes wireless network via Meraki AP through Catalyst Core toward internal servers; Palo Alto NGFW inspects traffic.

scenarios.title: SASE Cloud Ingress App Degradation & Synthetic Validation
scenarios.summary: Zscaler/Cloudflare edge proxy experiences SSL inspection latency surge; Palo Alto SD-WAN queues sessions and ThousandEyes detects SaaS TTFB slowdown.

scenarios.title: Mixed-Vendor Enterprise Network (Cisco, Arista, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Juniper, Aruba)
scenarios.summary: A perimeter scan and an application exploit attempt hit a multi-vendor enterprise: the Palo Alto firewall records the scan and blocks the exploit, the Fortinet firewall logs the same source in correlated flows, the nginx web tier shows the attempted request, and a Meraki access point raises a wireless alert from the same period. Normal traffic then resumes.

scenarios.title: Normal Operations (HTTP Round-Robin)
scenarios.summary: Legitimate external clients make distributed HTTP requests through a Cisco ASA, a Palo Alto firewall and an F5 load balancer to an nginx web tier backed by PostgreSQL. All events are normal: traffic is permitted, balanced across web nodes, and queries are parameterized.

scenarios.title: OpenConfig MDT Streaming & Telemetry Assurance
scenarios.summary: Routers and switches stream real-time OpenConfig YANG metrics (interface counters, CPU/RAM, BGP peering) directly to cisco_mdt_metrics.

scenarios.title: Pure Cisco Enterprise Fabric (Catalyst 9600, 9500, 9300, 9800, ISE, DNA-C)
scenarios.summary: Unified Cisco enterprise architecture spanning core, distribution, access, wireless, and identity. A rogue access point appears in an all-Cisco campus; Catalyst raises the rogue threat details, network-health samples are replayed, and the access-control layers (802.1X and TrustSec SGT) respond until the rogue is contained.

scenarios.title: Separate SD-WAN Environment Connected to Core Backbone (All Cisco)
scenarios.summary: A Catalyst SD-WAN branch edge peers with a Catalyst 9600 campus core. A transport brownout raises latency, jitter and loss on the primary circuit, the BGP session to the core flaps, application-aware routing steers traffic to the secondary circuit, and the tunnel SLA recovers.

scenarios.title: Service Provider Network - All Cisco (Cisco 8000, NCS 5500, IOS-XR SRv6)
scenarios.summary: Carrier-scale Cisco 8000 / NCS core running Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6).

scenarios.title: Service Provider Network - Mixed Vendor (Cisco 8000, Juniper PTX, Nokia 7750)
scenarios.summary: A Tier-1 transit core interconnects Cisco 8000, Juniper PTX and Nokia 7750 routers. A BGP peering de-synchronization across the vendor boundary causes an optical carrier loss on the Nokia port and an LSP fast-reroute on the Juniper router while Cisco telemetry shows the traffic shift; graceful restart and BFD dampening then stabilize the routing table.

scenarios.title: SQL Injection / Application Breach
scenarios.summary: Adversary injects malicious SQL exploitation payload through HTTP query parameters targeting Database backend.

scenarios.title: Enterprise Wireless Connected to Campus Core (All Cisco)
scenarios.summary: Catalyst 9800 WLC trunking wireless VLANs directly into Catalyst 9600 core switches. Catalyst wireless clients connect to the campus core; RF utilization climbs on a channel, a rogue access point is seen, and 802.1X authentication slows until the radio plan and policy recover.

scenarios.title: Enterprise Wireless Connected to Core (Mixed Vendor)
scenarios.summary: A Meraki access point serves corporate and guest clients behind a Palo Alto firewall. A guest client attempts to pivot toward data-center assets: the AP reports a rogue-probe alert, the firewall records the guest-to-datacenter attempts and applies its zero-trust deny, and guest traffic returns to normal internet-only flows.

scenarios.title: Windows Credential Compromise Kill Chain (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: Cross-Cloud Identity SSO Brute Force (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: AWS CloudTrail Recon & Escalation (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: Agentic AI Runtime Exfiltration Attempt (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: Kubernetes Auth Abuse + Container Escape (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: Network C2 Callback & Discovery Behaviors (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: Big-IP ADC & OpenConfig Observability Health (Wave-2 pack)

scenarios.title: eBPF Workload Hunt (Wave-3 pack)

scenarios.title: NetFlow: bandwidth saturation and elephant flows
scenarios.summary: Which few flows carry most of the bytes, who sends them, and how long do they last? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Utilization is shown only when you enter a link capacity; NetFlow carries no interface speed.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: QoS and DSCP marking validation
scenarios.summary: Is voice and video traffic marked with the DSCP the policy expects, and which endpoints are not? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Voice/video class comes from UDP port ranges (a heuristic); the policy (EF=46 voice, AF41=34 video) is the lab default, not discovered.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: routing-loop indicators (flow-only)
scenarios.summary: Are the same source/destination pairs being observed repeatedly across exporters and interfaces in a pattern a forwarding loop would produce? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Indicator only. NetFlow has no TTL, so TTL depletion and loop drops cannot be shown; ICMP time-exceeded or router counters would be needed to confirm.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: asymmetric-routing indicators
scenarios.summary: For which endpoint pairs is the reverse direction seen at a different exporter, or not seen at all? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. A missing reverse flow is not proof of asymmetry: sampling, observation coverage and collection gaps look the same. Pairs are classified as indicators.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: application baseline and duration drift
scenarios.summary: Did flow duration or volume to a destination drift away from its earlier baseline? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Flow duration is not application latency; it also depends on session length and exporter timeouts.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: volumetric DDoS indicators (SYN flood and UDP)
scenarios.summary: Where is the packet rate peaking, which protocols and TCP flags dominate, and which assets are targeted? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Synthetic flood patterns. Flow export may be sampled in production and cannot prove loss of availability.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: network reconnaissance and port scanning
scenarios.summary: Which hosts touch many ports or many destinations with tiny flows, and how does the footprint grow? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Connection attempts do not prove access. Approved vulnerability scanners produce the same pattern.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: outbound data-exfiltration indicators
scenarios.summary: Which internal host sends unusual byte volume to external destinations, and over what ports and times? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Volume alone does not establish data theft. Backups, updates and uploads look identical in flow data.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: command-and-control beaconing indicators
scenarios.summary: Which source/destination pairs reconnect on a regular interval, and how regular is it? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Periodicity is a weak indicator on its own: agents, monitoring and update checks beacon too. Encrypted payloads are not visible.

scenarios.title: NetFlow: DNS-tunneling indicators (flow-only, limited evidence)
scenarios.summary: Which clients send unusually many or unusually large DNS flows, and is request/response volume imbalanced? Synthetic flows from documentation address ranges. Limited evidence: flow data has no query names, lengths or entropy, so encoded labels cannot be detected here. Correlate with DNS logs for that.
